messages:
maya: Hey team — customer ACCT-776 reports their free-trial credits dropped from 10k to ~0 in the span of 20 minutes this morning. They run our `doc-sync` background worker every 1m to embed new docs into the index.

maya: Attached logs show a burst of calls to /v1/embeddings from the same org id with repeated request IDs. They say they didn't change anything.

sam: Can you paste a snippet of the worker request pattern? Are we seeing duplicate request bodies or different ids?

maya: Here's a cleaned log sample (timestamp order):

```
2026-03-16T08:12:01Z doc-sync[worker-1] INFO starting job job_id=abc123
2026-03-16T08:12:02Z doc-sync[worker-1] INFO POST /v1/embeddings 200 request_id=r1 tokens=1024
2026-03-16T08:12:02Z doc-sync[worker-2] INFO starting job job_id=abc123
2026-03-16T08:12:03Z doc-sync[worker-2] INFO POST /v1/embeddings 200 request_id=r2 tokens=1024
2026-03-16T08:12:03Z doc-sync[worker-3] INFO starting job job_id=abc123
2026-03-16T08:12:03Z doc-sync[worker-3] INFO POST /v1/embeddings 200 request_id=r3 tokens=1024
```

maya: So same job_id processed 3x concurrently, 3 embedding calls -> triple tokens charged.

lucas: Huh. That smells like scheduling/lease mismatch. Any recent deploys to the scheduler or memcache?

ops-bot: deploy-bot: rolled out commit 6f2a to services/doc-sync-scheduler at 2026-03-16T07:58:12Z

sam: We pushed a small change to heartbeat handling last night. If the scheduler lease expires early it might requeue the job and multiple workers could pick it up. Did the customer run across any transient infra issues?

maya: They said their worker host restarted once around 08:11, but they have 3 replicas and all showed start logs. No outages reported by infra.

sam: Two-pronged ask: (1) short-term mitigation for the customer + refund; (2) long-term fix in scheduler and forcing idempotency at the API. I can take (2).

lucas: For (1) we should grant them replacement trial credits matching the unexpected consumption and add a small buffer. Billing-Jane can approve.

billing-jane: I can issue a one-time 12k credit top-up and extend the trial by 10 days for ACCT-776. Confirm amount and I'll process.

maya: They were at ~10k, final balance ~20 after the burst. Loss ~9980 tokens. Suggest 11k to be safe.

billing-jane: Approved. I'll apply 11k promo credit and DM the customer.

sam: For the root cause, initial hypothesis: scheduler uses memcache lease with TTL=60s but our heartbeat interval increased to 65s after the change, so setnx TTL expired and job requeued while worker still processing -> parallel execution. Patch plan: lower TTL or make heartbeat sidecar update TTL, plus make job execution include `Idempotency-Key: job_id` header to /v1/embeddings so duplicates within window are deduped.

lucas: Also add server-side protection: if embeddings handler receives same org + idempotency-key + payload hash within 5m, respond with cached result (200) and mark as no-cost. We can implement quick guard using a Redis dedupe set keyed by org:idem:{key}. TTL 5m.

sam: I'll open PR with two commits: ensure scheduler heartbeat interval <= TTL and add Idempotency-Key header from worker. Also add a feature flag to enable server-side dedupe for embeddings.

maya: In the meantime, can support provide repro steps for engineering? Customer willing to let us run a short window with verbose logs.

lucas: Repro steps for them: (1) run two worker replicas with the same job schedule, (2) make worker artificially sleep 70s between heartbeats, (3) trigger a small doc set, (4) observe duplicate POSTs. I'll provide a small docker-compose sample if they want.

maya: They accepted. They also asked whether we can detect and refund automatically if we detect duplicate request_ids from same job_id cluster.

sam: We shouldn't rely on request_id alone. Better to dedupe on client-supplied Idempotency-Key. We'll add a retroactive detection script to scan logs for same job_id with multiple distinct request_ids within 30s and flag them for manual review — billing can auto-refund matches above threshold.

billing-jane: I'll accept a CSV of flagged incidents. If the script finds >1 duplicates for same job_id and payload hash, I'll auto-process refunds under an internal policy.

maya: Quick fixes applied: (1) issued 11k credit to ACCT-776, (2) set customer to monitoring mode + verbose logs, (3) told them to wait for dev PR and we scheduled a follow-up tomorrow.

sam: PR opened: https://git.redwood/infra/doc-sync/pull/452 (includes heartbeat fix + Idempotency-Key header + feature flag). Rolling to staging now.

lucas: Postmortem actions for our runbook: add scheduler TTL check to deploy validation, add test that simulates memcache eviction, and document worker-level idempotency requirement.

maya: Customer notified, appreciated fast response. They asked for ETA on server-side dedupe — give ~48h?

sam: ETA 48-72h for server-side guard behind feature flag, then a canary.

billing-jane: Done: promo credit 11000 applied to ACCT-776. I'll follow up with a note to CS. :white_check_mark:

maya: Thanks all. I'll close the support ticket once we've seen no reoccurrence for 24h.

lucas: One last note: add metrics for duplicate embeddings per org to our console so customers and we can spot this earlier.

maya: Noted. End of thread.
